paper.title: Pure exploration in multi-armed bandits with low rank structure using oblivious sampler

settings.name_in_paper: Pure exploration in multi-armed bandits with low rank reward and stochastic (time-varying) kernel, oblivious sampler
unmapped: Sampling strategy must be oblivious: the exploration distribution cannot depend on observed rewards (only the recommendation strategy sees feedback)
Rewards x_t = U_t v_t with i.i.d. random kernel U_t (N x d, revealed to the learner at the start of each round) and i.i.d. random seed vector v_t independent of U_t
Stopping time n is chosen by the environment (unknown to learner)
settings.definition_quote: A reward sequence $\bm{x}_1,\bm{x}_2,\cdots$ is said to have the low rank structure for the i.i.d. random kernel sequence $U_1,U_2,\cdots\in \mathbb{R}^{ N \times d}$ with $d \ll N$ if there are seed vector sequence ... such that $\bm{x}_t=U_t\bm{v}_t$ ... Finally, we assume that the kernel information $U_{t}$ is given to the algorithm in advance on each round

settings.name_in_paper: Pure exploration in multi-armed bandits with low rank reward and fixed kernel, oblivious sampler
unmapped: Sampling strategy must be oblivious (cannot use reward feedback)
Fixed kernel U (N x d) known to the learner; rewards x_t = U v_t with i.i.d. seed vectors v_t
Stopping time n is chosen by the environment (unknown to learner)
settings.definition_quote: For a $d$-rank reward sequence $\bm{x}_1,\bm{x}_2,\cdots$, there are a kernel matrix $U \in \mathbb{R}^{ N \times d}$ and $d$-dimensional vector sequence $\bm{v}_1,\bm{v}_2,\cdots$ such that $\bm{x}_t=U\bm{v}_t$ ... seed vector sequence is an i.i.d. random variable sequence that satisfies $\bm{v}_t\sim\mathcal{D}$, $U\bm{v}_t\in [-1,1]^N$

settings.name_in_paper: Pure exploration with low rank sequence, fixed kernel (lower bound)
unmapped: Fixed kernel U known to the learner; lower bound holds for both oblivious and adaptive samplers
settings.definition_quote: we assume that there are $N=2^{d}$ arms that each arm $\bm{u}_{i} \in \mathcal{A}=\lbrace +1, -1 \rbrace^{d}$ and seed vector $\bm{v}_{t} \in \mathcal{L}= \lbrace \pm\bm{e}_{i}: 1\leq i \leq d\rbrace$

settings.name_in_paper: Pure exploration in stochastic multi-armed bandits (lower bound)
settings.definition_quote: We assume that arm $i^{*}$ is  Bernoulli distributed with parameter $\frac{1+\epsilon}{2}$ and others with parameter $\frac{1-\epsilon}{2}$.

algorithms.name: Algorithm for pure exploration in stochastic kernel bandits (uniform oblivious sampling + averaged seed-vector estimator recommendation)
Uniform allocation over barycentric spanner arms + least-squares-type recommendation (fixed kernel)
C-approximate algorithm for pure exploration low rank bandits

symbols.alpha_U: max_t sup_{a,b in U} a^T A_t^{-1} b, A_t the exploration covariance
symbols.beta_U: upper bound on ||u_{t,i}|| ||v_t||_* for all t,i

conditions: kernel matrices U_t and seed vectors v_t are independent
kernel U_t revealed at start of each round

source.label: thm:regret-bound-time-varying
source.quote: In the pure exploration multi-armed bandits problem with time-varying kernel $U_{t} \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d}$ according to some underlying distribution. ... The simple regret $r_{n}$ ... is bounded: $\mathbb{E}[r_{n}] \leq O \left( \alpha \beta \sqrt{\frac{ \ln N}{n}} \right)$

results.notes: N arms mapped to K, stopping time n to T. Theorem stated for 'some exploration distribution p_t'; algorithm uses uniform. Proof is loose (McDiarmid applied with random I_s; epsilon choice inconsistent). Remark 1 states O(d sqrt(ln N/n)) when lambda_min(A_t) >= 1/4.

symbols.lam_min_A: max_t lambda_min(A_t), A_t the exploration covariance matrix

conditions: U (domain of kernel rows) is a finite subset of {0,1}^d
kernel matrices and seed vectors independent

source.label: thm:regret-bound-time-varying
source.quote: In particular, if $\mathcal{U}$ is a finite subset of $\lbrace 0,1 \rbrace^{d}$ we have further $\mathbb{E}[r_{n}] \leq O \left( d  \max_{t}\lbrace \lambda_{\min} (A_{t}) \rbrace\sqrt{\frac{ \ln N}{n}} \right)$, if $\beta \leq 1$.

results.notes: Recorded as printed; dependence on lambda_min (rather than its inverse) appears mathematically questionable.

conditions: kernel U is full rank and known
tuning: exact barycentric spanner (max-determinant subset) used for exploration

source.label: thm:regret-bound-fixed-kernel
source.quote: Running uniformly allocation to the selected $\lbrace i_{1},\cdots, i_{d}\rbrace \subseteq [N]$ arms ... We have an upper bound to the simple regret after $n$ times exploration: $\mathbb{E} \left[ r_{n} \right] \leq O \left(  \sqrt{\frac{ d^{2} \ln N }{ n }}  \right).$

results.notes: Exact barycentric spanner via max determinant is not stated to be polynomial; paper offers C-approximation (Proposition 1) for efficiency, so compute marked exponential for the exact version (uncertain). Remark 2: when d=N recovers O(sqrt(N ln N/n)).

symbols.C_apx: approximation factor of the C-approximate barycentric spanner oracle

conditions: kernel U known and full rank

source.quote: Running our algorithm for $n$ rounds, we have the upper bound to the simple regret as follows: $\mathbb{E}\left[ r_{n} \right] \leq O\left(  Cd \sqrt{\frac{  \ln N}{n}} \right)$

conditions: holds for both oblivious and adaptive samplers (Remark 3)

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: The lower bound to the simple regret for the multi-armed bandits with low rank sequence is $\Omega \left( \frac{d}{\sqrt{n}}\right),$ where the kernel matrix is a fixed $N \times d$ matrix.

results.notes: Proof reduces to two-armed subproblems via Lemma 1; argument is informal and scaling questionable.

conditions: holds for all recommendation strategies (oblivious or adaptive sampling)

source.quote: For all $N=2^{k}$, $ k \in \lbrace 1,\cdots, d \rbrace$ and all outputs of the recommendation strategy, there is a strategy of setting seed vector $\bm{v}_{t}$ such that $\mathbb{E}\left[ r_{n}  \right] \geq \Omega\left(  \sqrt{\frac{d \ln N}{n}} \right).$

results.notes: Seed vector construction cycles over blocks (not strictly i.i.d.); derived from Theorem 6.

conditions: Bernoulli arms with one arm (1+eps)/2 and the rest (1-eps)/2, good arm chosen uniformly

source.label: lem:lower-bound-multi-arm-pure-exploration
source.quote: The lower bound to the simple regret for the stochastic multi-armed bandits is $\Omega\left(\sqrt{\frac{N}{n}}\right)$.

results.notes: Restated as Theorem 7 in the supplementary material with the same bound. Proof sets eps = N/n, which appears inconsistent; well-known result.
